newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin says U.S. sought to impose hegemony on G7.
newsitem.headline: Jospin says U.S. sought to impose hegemony on G7.

text.p: Socialist French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin accused the United States on Tuesday of seeking to impose its economic and social model on Europe at last weekend's Group of Seven summit in Denver.

"I am not satisfied with the results of Denver...We see a certain tendency towards hegemony, which is not necessarily identical with exercising the global responsibilities of a great power, even if it is a friend," Jospin told parliament.
The prime minister did not attend the summit, at which France was represented by conservative President Jacques Chirac.
Jospin said Europe did not have the same model of society as the United States and had always tried to preserve a balance between economics and social priorities.
"Europe does not have the United States' attributes of power and the rules that may apply in the wake of that considerable power in the United States cannot be as effective in Europe," he said.

"It will be up to Europe's determination, and to France's own ability -- and my government will work to that end -- to ensure that Europe's concerns carry greater weight next time perhaps," Jospin added.

The prime minister did not directly criticise Chirac's performance at the summit. He said he had not attended himself because he was not interested in "formal representative roles", and that Socialist finance and foreign ministers had accompanied the president "because we did not want him to be alone".
The G7 summit urged Europe's three biggest economies -- Germany, France and Italy -- to carry out structural reforms to combat their high unemployment.

In Denver, Chirac rejected attempts to apply the American model of economic deregulation and welfare reduction to solve Europe's problem of high unemployment and slow growth, saying he remained attached to the European social model.
Discussing his own role, Jospin said: "I will not go where my presence is not formally required, but I will go where the policy of the French government has to be put into effect."
